_readme: The fleet's one comment grammar: what a teammate's comment on a task ASKS FOR.
Compiled by agents/comment-grammar.mjs and design/comment_grammar.py from these
very strings, so the two languages cannot drift — they did (fleet loop task
on 2026-09-11, five of sixteen real phrases were read differently by
the deck (Python) and the demo/SDR (JS) classifiers, and the dangerous direction
was the silent no-op — 'send as-is' on a parked demo meant nothing was sent while
the writer believed they had approved it.
Patterns use only syntax both engines read identically: (?:...), \s, \b, [\s\S].
No named groups, no lookbehind, no \d{2,} quantifier tricks. Each is matched
against the WHOLE comment (anchored ^...$), which is what stops "don't send yet"
matching "send". Adding a verb is a change to this file plus a fixture.
Order matters: send, then send_with_text, then retry; anything else is steer.

send.means: Ship the parked thing as it stands — the deck, the demo video, the drafted reply.

send_with_text.means: Ship it, but with the human's own words as the cover note or reply body — used verbatim, never re-drafted.

retry.means: Rebuild it. The text after the verb, when there is any, is the guidance for the rebuild.

fallback.means: Anything else a teammate wrote: context for the next attempt, never an instruction to send. The whole comment is the payload.
